passage.title: Muslim, from Umar (the hadith of Jibril)
paras: Iman is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in the decree, its good and its bad.

rows: Allah knows, writes, wills and creates all

Meaning

keywords.def: belief in the heart, said with the tongue and shown in actions

questions.q: Explain what belief in qadar means.
questions.a: Allah knows everything, wrote it, wills it and creates it; we still choose and are responsible.

questions.q: The last of the messengers is ...
How many pillars of iman are there?
Iman organiser on the pupil PDF: each pillar with meaning, evidence and 'how it changes how I live'.
questions.a: Six rows with accurate meaning, evidence and a practical effect

questions.q: Extend: why is iman described as increasing and decreasing?
questions.a: Good deeds increase it; sins weaken it (scholars draw this from texts such as 48:4).

questions.q: Stretch: how does the hadith of Jibril connect Islam, iman and ihsan?
questions.a: Three levels: actions, beliefs, and worshipping Allah as if you see Him.

questions.q: Which is a pillar of iman, not of Islam?
questions.a: A) Belief in the angels. Angels are a pillar of iman; salah and zakah are pillars of Islam.

questions.q: Belief in the Last Day is a pillar of ...
Think again: how can you tell iman is there?
questions.a: It shows in words and actions.
